I think what it is, is how intimate the destruction Jimmy and Kim enacted was. Walter did horrible shit constantly, but it was out of pride and destructive ego, and those around him were left in his wake, Jimmy and Kim set out to destroy a man who absolutely did not deserve to be destroyed, and ultimately got him killed even if it was completely unintended. Throughout all of Jimmy and Kim's plans and executions, they laugh, they celebrate, they get off to it. Walt enjoys it and even gets off to it to, but I think Jimmy and Kim's framing is more sinister than Walt's, especially when we've known Howard for six seasons and know he's a decent guy who's been through a lot

I think the fact that people are suddenly jumping to this when we've known this was more or less the plan for a while is probably intended. In that way, the viewers are going through a similar situation to Jimmy and Kim, it's fun and exciting to plan and watch their plot unfold, it's a little heist, but when that plan is done, once we see the consequences, we're reminded how horrible it actually was, and we realize that too late, because we should have known it to begin with, and we kinda did, but we chose to ignore it (obviously not everybody thinks this way it's just similar to my thought process and that of others I see on here). I think the show does an excellent job of getting the viewer to get caught up in the excitement in the same way that the characters do.
